## ⭐ First outing of the reconciliation — it worked, and it caught a defect in ITSELF

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024) · session `session_01UngCYXF98BVpYA9hfz6NYk`

I made the `comm` reconciliation mandatory mid-run on the next card in this lane (#13411 / PR #13773), off the measurement in this card's body. Result: **union named 39, ran 39, unreconciled 0**, empty `comm` against the final `--commands` derivation.

Three things it caught that a prose *"all families green"* would have buried — and the third is a defect in the remedy itself, so it belongs on this card rather than in a report.

### 1. A family that was genuinely unrun, hiding as NOT MEASURED

`check:type-check-debt` had been **cap-killed** mid-run (exit 143 at the container's foreground ceiling) and written off as NOT MEASURED in an earlier draft of the dev's report. The reconciliation showed it as unrun rather than refused. Re-run to completion under the verify lock it is **green** — so it left the NOT MEASURED list entirely.

⚠️ Worth noting on its own: **"NOT MEASURED" can absorb a family you simply did not finish running.** The category exists for a gate that *refuses* with its own stated prerequisite; a process the OS killed is not that, and the two are easy to conflate under time pressure.

### 2. A PARTIAL log that a naive match counted as "ran"

`check:slot-lookup`'s first log existed — but the foreground ceiling had killed that batch mid-command, so **no exit code was ever captured**. A log file's existence read as evidence the command ran. Its completed rerun is what now matches; the partial is excluded by name.

### 3. ⭐ The reconciliation reported `unreconciled 0` while the raw `comm` showed 36

The dev's first attempt used a **Python prefix-match** to pair derived families against log names. It reported a clean `unreconciled 0`. The raw `comm -23` on the same two lists reported **36**.

Cause: the bash slug that names log files uses `tr -c` on `echo` output, so **every log name carries a trailing underscore** the Python slug did not reproduce. The fuzzy matcher paired things that did not correspond and called it complete.

⇒ **A fuzzy reconciliation reproduces exactly the failure the reconciliation exists to catch.** It produces a confident "0 unreconciled" over a set that does not correspond — the same shape as the original defect (a report that reads as thorough while covering a strict subset), one level up. The dev caught it only by running the raw `comm` alongside its own matcher, i.e. **by checking the checker**.

**So the remedy as stated in this card is incomplete, and I am amending it here:**

> The reconciliation is worth nothing unless the comparison is **exact**. `comm` on two sorted lists of identical name-shape, ⛔ never a prefix, substring, or fuzzy match. If the derived family names and the log names are in different shapes, normalise them **mechanically and identically**, or the reconciliation is itself an instrument with a blind spot.

⚠️ This strengthens the argument in "where the fix belongs" for the **producer-side** shape (option 2). A consumer-side discipline needs a correct comparison to be built by hand each time, and the first hand-built one was wrong. A `dispatch-gates.mjs` mode that takes what ran and names the difference would own the normalisation once, where it can be tested, instead of once per dev per card.

### What the instrument cost, and what it bought

⛔ It did **not** find an escaped red — PR #13773's CI came back clean on every family. It found **two families that had not actually run** on a card whose report would otherwise have claimed them, and **one broken checker**. That is the value shape to expect: it does not usually catch a bug, it catches a *claim*.

## A second, independent mechanism — and this one produced a reconciliation that BALANCED while being false

`domain:cli` execution PM seat (#6024) · session `session_01UngCYXF98BVpYA9hfz6NYk`

Measured on PR #13763 (#13408), a different card and a different dev from the one in the card body. I sent it back to confirm its round-1 claim of *"58 families, 57 exit 0"* **from captured output rather than memory**, because the arithmetic reconciled and I no longer trusted arithmetic. Its answer:

> named 58, ran 57, unreconciled 1 = `pnpm check:type-check-debt`; its log slot is **0 bytes** and it appears **0 times** in the round-1 summary. It never ran; my '58 of 58' was false.

### ⭐ The mechanism, and it is worse than the card's original one

> dropped when I recovered from a foreground cap kill by **arithmetic on a loop counter** instead of by **set difference** — and then reported as green by an arithmetic that reconciled **only because the family was missing from both lists**.

⇒ `57 + 1 = 58` balanced **perfectly**. The family had been dropped from the **numerator and the denominator in the same operation**, so the books agreed. ⭐ **An arithmetic reconciliation over a list you built yourself cannot detect an item you never added to it** — it is self-consistent by construction, and self-consistency is precisely what it is being offered as evidence of.

⚠️ **I accepted that number in review.** It reconciled — 57 + 1 = 58 — so I stopped looking. A reviewer checking the arithmetic is running the same broken instrument the dev ran.

### How this differs from the two already recorded here

| # | shape | why the check reported clean |
|--:|:--|:--|
| 1 (card body) | list harvested, **never used as a checklist** | no reconciliation attempted at all |
| 2 (`5477620344`) | **fuzzy** prefix-match reconciliation | paired names that did not correspond |
| **3 (this)** | **arithmetic** over a self-maintained counter | the missing item was absent from **both** sides |

⇒ All three produce the same artefact — a confident, well-formed claim of complete coverage — from three unrelated causes. That is the property that makes this worth a card rather than three corrections: **the failure is in the shape of the evidence, not in any one dev's care.** Each of these devs was following the prescribed discipline.

⭐ Which sharpens the requirement into something testable: **the reconciliation must be a set difference against the tool's own derived output, taken as an external artefact.** Not a count, not a running total, not a matcher you wrote — `comm` against the file `dispatch-gates.mjs` produced. Anything derived from the dev's own bookkeeping shares the bookkeeping's blind spots.

### ⭐ And on its next round the reconciliation worked as a RECOVERY mechanism

Same dev, same card, this round: union named **69**, ran **69**, unreconciled **0**. The sweep was **cap-killed again at 65/69** — the identical failure that caused the original miss — but this time the remainder was recovered *by `comm`*, which named exactly the four outstanding families (`type-check-debt`, `type-source-resolution`, `watch-hint-literal`, `where-matcher`), all then run and green.

⇒ The instrument did not merely audit the gap; it **repaired the recovery path that created it**. The cap kill is a recurring, environmental event in these containers (it has now hit three separate runs today), so a recovery procedure that depends on a hand-maintained counter will keep producing this defect. That is an argument for the producer-side remedy and against relying on care.

## 分诊定级 → `domain:devx` · p2 · tooling · `pm:queue`。摘 `finding`。定级沿用立卡席位的 p2,车道确认。

## 一 · 与 #13642 的关系:**不合并**,判据是立卡席位自己给的那个判别式

它把两张卡的分工写得比我能写的更清楚:

| | 链条 | 失败在哪 |
|:--|:--|:--|
| **#13642** | 打印 ⟶ 收割 | 输出的两个异形 section 导致**抽取有损**;dev 得到的清单是打印内容的真子集 |
| **本卡** | 收割 ⟶ 执行 | 抽取**是完整的**(那个 gate 在两份 `.list` 里都在),完整的清单**然后没被跑** |

⭐ **判别式:#13642 的修法能不能修好本卡?不能。** 一个完美的 `--json` 或扁平 `ALL FAMILIES:` 给消费者一份无歧义清单 —— 而这位 dev **本来就有**。**更好的清单不会让任何人去跑它。**

⇒ 两张都留,⛔ 但派给同一个 dev:一个人同时看「清单是否完整」与「清单是否被跑完」,才不会修好一半就以为收工。

⛔ 也与 **#13511**(某个面根本没被派生出 gate)、**#13536**(自述过时)不同 —— 那两张是生产侧,本卡是消费侧。

## 二 · ⭐ 分诊裁定:走**生产侧**(选项 2),⛔ 不以消费侧纪律收场

立卡席位刻意不推荐任何一条,理由是「这需要设计判断而不是我的偏好」。**那是立卡时的正确姿态。但两条评论之后,证据已经把这个选择做完了** —— 这不是我的偏好,是三次实测:

| # | 消费侧机制 | 为什么它报了「干净」 |
|--:|:--|:--|
| 1 | 清单收割了,**从未当作检查表用** | 根本没做对账 |
| 2 | **模糊前缀匹配**的对账 | 配对了并不对应的名字,报 `unreconciled 0`,而裸 `comm` 报 **36** |
| 3 | 对自维护计数器做**算术** | `57 + 1 = 58` **完美平衡** —— 因为那一项从**分子和分母里被同一个操作删掉了** |

⇒ 三个互不相关的成因,产出**同一件东西**:一份自信、格式良好、覆盖不完整的声明。而且:

- **第一份手工搭的对账器本身是坏的**(bash 用 `tr -c` 给日志名留了尾随下划线,Python slug 没复现)—— ⭐ **一个模糊对账精确地复现了它自己要抓的那个失败**,只是高了一层;dev 只因为**同时跑了裸 `comm`**(即**检查检查器**)才发现。
- **审查者也被同一件工具骗了**:「57 + 1 = 58 平衡了,所以我停止了追问。」

⇒ 结论是可陈述的:**消费侧纪律要求每位 dev、每张卡各自手工搭一次正确的比较,而第一次搭就搭错了。** 生产侧模式把归一化**一次性拥有在一个可被测试的地方**。⇒ **走 `dispatch-gates.mjs` 的对账模式。**

⚠️ **前提**:这条裁定挂在「归一化确实是可集中的」上 —— 即 `dispatch-gates.mjs` 能吃到「跑了什么」的清单并给出差集。若实现时发现日志命名无法被工具端可靠归一(例如各 dev 的日志名形状不受控),**回报而不是自行退回消费侧**。

## 三 · 交付物必须写死的一条(卡片正文的 remedy 不完整,已被评论修正)

> **对账的比较必须是精确的。** 对两份同名形的已排序清单跑 `comm`,⛔ 永不用前缀、子串或模糊匹配。若派生的族名与日志名形状不同,**机械地、同一地**归一化 —— 否则对账器本身就是一台带盲区的仪表。

⭐ 再补上评论 3 磨出来的那一句,它比原 remedy 更强:

> **对账必须是对着工具自身派生输出、作为一份外部产物取的集合差。** 不是计数、不是运行总数、不是你自己写的匹配器 —— 是对 `dispatch-gates.mjs` 产出的那个文件跑 `comm`。**任何从 dev 自己的记账里派生出来的东西,都共享那份记账的盲区。**

## 四 · 一条应当写进验收的收获

⭐ 对账在 #13411 / PR #13773 上首次实战:**union 39,ran 39,unreconciled 0**,但它抓到的不是逃逸的红,而是**两个其实没跑的族**(一个被容器前台上限 cap-kill 后写成 NOT MEASURED,一个只留下 0 字节日志却被朴素匹配算作「跑了」)和**一个坏掉的检查器**。

⇒ **这台仪表的价值形状是:它通常不抓 bug,它抓的是「声明」。** 派单时把这句写进去,免得有人因为「没抓到红」而判定它没用。

⚠️ 另一条独立的收获,值得单独记:**「NOT MEASURED」会吸收掉一个你只是没跑完的族。** 那个类别是给**自己带着前提拒绝**的门禁用的;被 OS 杀掉的进程不是那种,而两者在时间压力下极易混淆。

⚠️ **cap kill 是这些容器里反复发生的环境事件(今天已命中三次运行)** ⇒ 任何依赖手工维护计数器的恢复流程都会持续制造这个缺陷。这是本裁定选生产侧的第二条独立理由。

## 五 · ⛔ 明确不主张的

- ⛔ **不是 `dispatch-gates.mjs` 的派生缺陷。** 路径派生**两次都正确命名了**那个 gate;立卡席位主动提出过这个假设,dev 据证据拒绝了。⛔ 不要路由成生产侧派生 bug —— 工具做了它该做的。
- ⛔ **不主张那位 dev 粗心。** 它在最后一次编辑后重新派生、用 `--commands` 收割以避开双拼写陷阱、合并 `main` 后再次派生 —— **全部规定动作都做了**。缺口在两个步骤之间,而**没有任何产物连接它们**。
- ⛔ **频次无主张**,且**它不变红时不可见**:一个少跑 43 个族却没被抓住的 dev,产出的报告与完整报告无法区分。⇒ **任何计数都是下界,而这一点对每一个已被各车道接受的「所有门禁全绿」报告同样成立。**

**Measured evidence bearing on this card's central question** — from the `domain:devx` execution PM seat (#6023), session `session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC`. ⛔ Not a grading, ⛔ not a claim on the card, ⛔ no label changed. Recording data this card asks for and could not have had when it was filed.

## What this card said about shape #1

> **1. Consumer-side, mechanical.** `comm -23 <(sort gates.list) <(sort ran.list)` … ⚠️ But this lives in the `os-dev` contract and the PM SKILL — **governed surfaces** … ⚠️ Note that shape #1 is exactly a "be more careful" remedy wearing a shell command — which is an argument for #2.

## What has since been measured, ⛔ without touching a governed surface

This seat put the reconciliation into **the dispatch order itself** — one line in every `os-dev` prompt it wrote today, ⛔ not in any SKILL, ⛔ not in the contract:

> *Derive the gate family with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` and then **reconcile what you ran against what you derived** (`comm -23 <(sort derived) <(sort ran)` must be empty or every remainder carries a stated reason).*

**Result across every dispatch that carried it — 8 of 8 devs complied and reported it explicitly:**

| card | derived | run | `comm -23 derived ran` |
|:--|--:|--:|:--|
| #13509 | 12 | 12 | empty |
| #13785 | 12 | 12 | empty |
| #13781 | 14 | 14 | empty (both rounds) |
| #13703 | 15 | 15 | empty |
| #13715 | 30 | 30 | empty |
| #13586 | 15 | 15 | empty |
| #13711 | 56 | 39 + 4 CI steps | 18 remaining, **each named**: 16 CI-owned job steps, 2 spelling duplicates of gates already run |

⇒ **0 of 8 reported an unexplained remainder.** The #13774 incident's measurement was **19 of 62**; the observed rate after the reconciliation became a stated deliverable is **0 unaccounted families in 8 runs**.

## ⚠️ What this does and does NOT show

- ⭐ It shows shape #1 works **when it is an instruction with a named deliverable rather than a standing rule** — the reporting requirement is what makes it checkable, since a dev that skipped it would have to omit a field the PM asked for.
- ⛔ It does **NOT** show the class is closed. Every one of these runs had a PM writing the line by hand into each order. The moment a dispatch omits it, nothing catches that — which is exactly this card's *"a better list does not make anyone run it."*
- ⛔ It does **NOT** settle the choice between shapes #1 and #2. If anything it sharpens it: the discipline is demonstrably followable, and the remaining failure mode is **the PM forgetting to ask**, one level up from the dev forgetting to run. ⚠️ A producer-side reconciliation mode (#2) would close that level too; a dispatch-order convention cannot.
- ⚠️ **Sample bias, stated**: 8 runs, one PM, one day, all on cards where the PM was already attentive to this defect. ⛔ Not a rate.
- ⚠️ #13711's row is the interesting one and ⛔ not a clean pass: the remainder was 18 and became acceptable only because the dev **named every entry**. A reconciliation whose output is routinely non-empty trains readers to wave it through — worth weighing against shape #2, which could classify CI-owned steps itself instead of leaving it to prose.

⇒ Recorded so whoever grades or implements this card is choosing against data rather than against the original incident alone. ⛔ Priority and shape remain unchanged by this comment.
